svg.title: Sticky routing before the session was removed, and round-robin routing after
svg.desc: Two panels side by side with identical internal layout, so only the wiring differs. On the left, until revision 2025-11-25: the client sends an Mcp-Session-Id header, drawn struck through, and the balancer is pinned by a single arrow to replica one, which holds that session. Replicas two and three are greyed out and marked unusable. On the right, from revision 2026-07-28: the client sends _meta carrying its version and capabilities, and the balancer draws three arrows, marked round robin, one to each of three identical replicas. Notes below each panel say that restarting the pinned replica killed the conversation, and that restarting any replica now costs one retry, with state that must outlive a call carried in a server-minted handle passed back as an ordinary tool argument.
svg.text: The session was the thing that stopped a server from scaling
Remove the one field that had to be remembered, and the routing constraint goes with it.
One replica holds the session. The balancer has no choice.
Restart replica 1 and the conversation dies with it.
Scaling out adds capacity nobody can reach.
The handshake had to happen before any real work.
Every request carries its own context. Any replica answers.
Restart any replica and the next request lands elsewhere.
State that must outlive a call becomes a server-minted
handle, passed back as an ordinary tool argument.
The struck-out header is removed, not optional. There is no session to resume.
